title: Characteristic quotient of the logarithmic cotangent fibre over a trivial log field
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $f:(X,M)\to(\operatorname{Spec}F,F^\times)$ be a morphism to the trivial log field. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$, put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and let $C=(M_{\bar x}/A^\times)^{\rm gp}$ be the group completion of its characteristic monoid. Use the logarithmic differential module $\omega_{f,\bar x}$ of [def-per-log-differential-stalk]. There is a canonical surjective $k$-linear map
$$\pi:k\otimes_A\omega_{f,\bar x}\longrightarrow k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C$$
with $\pi(1\otimes d\log m)=1\otimes[m]$ for every $m\in M_{\bar x}$ and $\pi(1\otimes da)=0$ for every $a\in A$. In particular these formulas are well defined on the differential relations and on the quotient by units. Log smoothness is not required. Tensor products and scalar extension have their usual module meanings [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, canonical map (1) and its surjectivity; its formula is a consequence of the differential relations and does not require log smoothness. No Stacks tag states this logarithmic assertion.

proof.text: Use A = strictLocalRing X t and its actual quotient k = A / Ideal.span {a | not IsUnit a} from [def-per-log-cotangent-comparison]. Every nonunit maps to zero by Ideal.subset_span and Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem. This calculation needs neither an affine-neighbourhood comparison nor a separate locality theorem.

Write $L=M_{\bar x}$ and $T=k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}C$, with its usual $k$-module structure and $A$-action $a\cdot t=\rho(a)t$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. The quotient and group-completion presentation of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives a monoid-to-additive-group homomorphism $c:L\to C$ satisfying $c(mm')=c(m)+c(m')$ and $c(u)=0$ for $u\in A^\times$. Let $E$ be the free $A$-module on the symbols $da$ and $d\log m$ used in [def-per-log-differential-stalk]. Define an $A$-linear map $h_0:E\to T$ by $h_0(da)=0$ and $h_0(d\log m)=1\otimes c(m)$: explicitly apply these prescriptions termwise to a finite formal sum, reducing each coefficient by $\rho$. This definition has no choices of charts or representatives of characteristic classes.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, construction and surjectivity of map (1), with the differential-relation checks expanded.

proof.text: Check the additive, Leibniz and multiplicative-log relations of [def-per-log-differential-stalk]. Both $h_0(d(a+b)-da-db)$ and $h_0(d(ab)-a\,db-b\,da)$ are zero because every ordinary symbol is sent to zero. For $m,n\in L$ the image of $d\log(mn)-d\log m-d\log n$ is $1\otimes(c(mn)-c(m)-c(n))=0$, using the group-completion relations of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. In particular the logarithmic identity symbol also maps to zero.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, construction and surjectivity of map (1), with the differential-relation checks expanded.

proof.text: For dα(m) − α(m)dlog(m), split on IsUnit (α(m)). In the nonunit case its residue is zero by the explicit quotient in [def-per-log-cotangent-comparison]. In the unit case reflectsUnits in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] makes m a unit; Associates.mk_eq_one makes c(m)=0. Thus h₀ kills the structural relation of [def-per-log-differential-stalk].

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, construction and surjectivity of map (1), with the differential-relation checks expanded.

proof.text: For the base log relations of [def-per-log-differential-stalk], construct the monoid map N_(f(t)) → M_t directly by the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]: pull each pointed base neighbourhood back along f, apply sectionMap and then germ. Naturality of f.sectionMap and the pointed colimit equations make this a cocone. For any relative diagram V → W the comparison V → X ×_Y W and naturality show that the image of germ_W(b) is germ_V(f.sectionMap(b)). Since the triviality locus is all of the base, Associates (N_(f(t))) is subsingleton; hence every base germ is a unit by Associates.mk_eq_one. The constructed monoid map preserves its inverse. Thus every base logarithmic generator has zero characteristic class. Base ordinary generators already map to zero.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, construction and surjectivity of map (1), with the differential-relation checks expanded.

proof.text: The preceding checks show that $h_0$ kills the $A$-span of every defining relation, so it descends to an $A$-linear map $h:\omega_{f,\bar x}\to T$ through the explicit quotient of [def-per-log-differential-stalk]: two representatives differ by a finite $A$-linear sum of the checked relations and have equal images. Define $\pi(b\otimes w)=b\,h(w)$ for $b\in k$. The pairing is additive in each variable and $A$-balanced, since $b\,h(aw)=b\rho(a)h(w)$. The tensor-product construction of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore induces a map on $k\otimes_A\omega_{f,\bar x}$. It is $k$-linear, since multiplying the first tensor factor by $b_0\in k$ multiplies its value by $b_0$, as in [def-weil-module-base-change]. Its values are precisely $\pi(1\otimes da)=0$ and $\pi(1\otimes d\log m)=1\otimes c(m)$.

source.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, construction and surjectivity of map (1), with the differential-relation checks expanded.

proof.text: By the group-completion presentation of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], every $g\in C$ is a finite integer sum $g=\sum_j n_jc(m_j)$ with $m_j\in L$. Thus each pure tensor $b\otimes g\in T$ has the preimage $\sum_j(bn_j)\otimes d\log m_j$ under $\pi$. Pure tensors generate $T$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and sums of their displayed preimages give a preimage for every element. Hence $\pi$ is surjective. Finally the symbols $da,d\log m$ generate the presented module [def-per-log-differential-stalk], so their tensors with $1$ generate its scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change]; the prescribed values uniquely determine $\pi$. This proves canonicity as well as existence. The argument nowhere uses log smoothness, log regularity or perfection of $F$.

proof_origin.place: Expose X proof of Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--137, map (1) and its surjectivity; relation checks expanded using the explicit LogDifferential presentation. The residue quotient kills nonunits by definition, so the affine strict-henselization comparison and locality lemmas are unnecessary. The base-log check constructs the stalk map from pointed pullbacks and naturality. Surjectivity uses the fraction presentation of GrothendieckGroup; uniqueness uses quotient and Finsupp induction.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_logCotangent_characteristicQuotient_of_trivialBase {F : Type u} [Field F] (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (N : EtaleLogStructure (Spec (.of F))) (hN : N.IsFineSaturated) (f : EtaleLogHom X ⟨Spec (.of F), inferInstance, N, hN⟩) (htriv : N.trivialityLocus = Set.univ) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) : ∃! π : LogCotangentTarget f t →ₗ[logCotangentResidue t] TensorProduct ℤ (logCotangentResidue t) (Additive (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (X.logStructure.characteristic t))), Function.Surjective π ∧ (∀ m : X.logStructure.stalk t, π (TensorProduct.tmul (strictLocalRing X.scheme t) 1 (f.logDLog t m)) = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ 1 (Additive.ofMul (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (Associates.mk m)))) ∧ ∀ a : strictLocalRing X.scheme t, π (TensorProduct.tmul (strictLocalRing X.scheme t) 1 (f.logD t a)) = 0
